name: Vancomycin
summary: Intravenous vancomycin needs kidney-based dose adjustment guided by serum concentrations. The US label sets an initial dose of no less than 15 mg/kg at any level of kidney function, then dosing by measured levels. The 2020 consensus guideline recommends weight-based loading that is not reduced for kidney function and area-under-the-curve (AUC) guided maintenance (target 400 to 600 mg·h/L).
kidney_function_basis: Label gives no fixed eGFR or CrCl bands; dosing is concentration-guided.

bands.recommendation: 15–20 mg/kg (actual body weight) every 8–12 hours; AUC-guided (target 400–600 mg·h/L) (Rybak 2020). Label alternative: 2 g/day (0.5 g every 6 hours or 1 g every 12 hours), adjusted to serum concentrations.

Loading dose is not reduced for kidney function: 20–35 mg/kg actual body weight (maximum 3 g) if critically ill (Rybak 2020). Then extend the interval and adjust maintenance by AUC or serum concentrations (label: initial dose no less than 15 mg/kg).

Loading dose is not reduced for kidney function: 20–35 mg/kg actual body weight (maximum 3 g) if critically ill (Rybak 2020). Maintenance by AUC or serum concentrations (label: initial dose no less than 15 mg/kg).

Loading dose is not reduced for kidney function: 20–35 mg/kg actual body weight (maximum 3 g) if critically ill (Rybak 2020). Functionally anephric (label): 15 mg/kg initially, then about 1.9 mg/kg every 24 hours; guide further doses by serum concentrations.

hd.text: Rybak 2020 (Rec 13; mg/kg, maintenance three times weekly): dose given after HD ends: load 25 mg/kg, then 7.5 mg/kg (low-permeability dialyzer) or 10 mg/kg (high-permeability). Dose given during HD (intradialytic): load 30 mg/kg (low-permeability) or 35 mg/kg (high-permeability), then 7.5–10 mg/kg (low) or 10–15 mg/kg (high). Loading by actual body weight, maximum 3,000 mg (Rec 11). Adjust to pre-dialysis concentrations: 15–20 mg/L is likely to give AUC 400–600 mg·h/L; check at least weekly (Rec 14).
hd.short: Load; redose each HD; pre-HD level 15–20

pd.text: PD peritonitis: intraperitoneal vancomycin per the ISPD 2022 guideline (weight-based intermittent dosing; redose guided by serum levels); see the guideline for doses. Vancomycin enters peritoneal dialysis fluid (label). Specialist input.

crrt.text: Load 20–25 mg/kg actual body weight, then 7.5–10 mg/kg every 12 hours at effluent 20–25 mL/kg/h; guide maintenance by serum concentrations within the first 24 hours (Rybak 2020, Rec 16).

dialyzable: Yes with high-flux HD (substantial removal each session; the label's 'poorly removed' statement reflects older low-flux membranes). Give maintenance doses after HD or during the last part of the session.
monitoring: Serum concentrations (AUC-guided, target 400–600 mg·h/L, per consensus; trough per label); pre-dialysis levels at least weekly on hemodialysis; serum creatinine; nephrotoxicity risk rises with other nephrotoxins.

pediatric.approved_ages: IV: pediatric patients under 18 years for the labeled infections (label 1.1–1.5, 8.4).
pediatric.usual_dose: 3 months and older, normal kidney function, serious MRSA: 60–80 mg/kg/day divided every 6–8 hours, AUC-guided (Rybak 2020, Rec 17). Label: 10 mg/kg every 6 hours (1 month and older).
pediatric.max_dose: Usually 3,600 mg/day empirically; most children should not need more than 3,000 mg/day; check levels early when doses exceed 2,000–3,000 mg/day (Rybak 2020, Rec 18).

renal.recommendation: ≥3 months, serious MRSA: 60–80 mg/kg/day divided every 6–8 hours, AUC-guided (Rybak 2020). Label: 10 mg/kg every 6 hours.
Reduce the dose for kidney impairment and guide by AUC (preferably Bayesian) or serum concentrations (Rybak 2020, Rec 19–20). Label: initial dose no less than 15 mg/kg, then by levels.

hd.text: No pediatric dialysis or CRRT recommendation in the label or Rybak 2020; dose by levels with specialist (pediatric nephrology/infectious diseases) input.

pd.text: No pediatric dialysis or CRRT recommendation in the label or Rybak 2020; dose by levels with specialist (pediatric nephrology/infectious diseases) input.

crrt.text: No pediatric dialysis or CRRT recommendation in the label or Rybak 2020; dose by levels with specialist (pediatric nephrology/infectious diseases) input.

pediatric.neonates: Neonates (label): initial 15 mg/kg, then 10 mg/kg every 12 hours in the first week of life and every 8 hours thereafter up to 1 month of age.
pediatric.notes: Target AUC 400 mg·h/L, potentially up to 600, in children; keep AUC below 800 and trough below 15 mg/L to limit acute kidney injury; avoid 100 mg/kg/day or more (Rec 21). Monitoring may begin within 24–48 hours (Rec 20). Nonobese children: insufficient data for a loading dose (Rec 22). Obese children: loading 20 mg/kg total body weight (Rec 24). Neonates and infants up to 3 months: 10–20 mg/kg every 8–48 hours by postmenstrual age, weight and serum creatinine (Rec 25).
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)

pirrt.text: Hybrid HD (PIRRT/SLED): load 20–25 mg/kg actual body weight; do not delay the first dose until the session ends; then 15 mg/kg after each session or during its final 60–90 minutes (Rybak 2020, Rec 15).

revision_log.change: ≥60 band uses weight-based 15–20 mg/kg q8–12h, AUC-guided; label 2 g/day as alternative.
CKD bands state the loading dose is not reduced (20–35 mg/kg if critically ill).
Dialyzability and HD rewritten for high-flux HD with Rybak 2020 pre-HD level strategy; HD tile amber.
Removed 'reviewer to transcribe'/'see notes' drafting text from published fields.
CRRT dosing per Rybak 2020 item 16 (and hybrid item 15); tile amber.
PD pointer to ISPD 2022 intraperitoneal dosing (exact mg/kg not published: not verifiable here).
Pediatric dosing per Rybak 2020 (60–80 mg/kg/day; max 3,600 mg/day); drafting note replaced.
